claim: Guijarro-Ordonez, Pelger and Zanotti (Deep Learning Statistical Arbitrage, arXiv 2106.04028): on about 550 liquid US stocks, out of sample 2002-2016, the Sharpe ratio of the learned residual stat-arb policy has a half-life of about seven trading days over the holding period, is still above one at a 22-day holding period with a 1-day objective, and reaches about 1.5 when the multi-day holding period is optimized directly (Figure 12).
impact_on_spec: Sets the trading-speed grid (kappa 1..0.05, full rebalance every 5 or 21 sessions) and the lag range 1..22 of the decay curve; Stage 1 of P1 replicates this model.
independent_replication: One independent partial replication (bsiranosian blog); the only 2016-2024 replication (arXiv 2412.11432) was withdrawn.
limitations: Authors' backtest, ends 2016, 5 bp per transaction plus 1 bp short fee; learned signal, not the linear library signals measured here.
quote: The half-life in terms of Sharpe ratios is around seven trading days. In fact, the Sharpe ratio is still above one with a one month (22 business days) holding period

claim: Da, Liu and Schaumburg (NY Fed Staff Report 513; Management Science 2014): the standard short-term reversal profit decomposes into across-industry momentum, within-industry expected-return variation, under-reaction to within-industry cash-flow news and a residual; only the residual is significant and positive, and a strategy built to capture it earns a risk-adjusted return three times the standard reversal over 1982-2009.
impact_on_spec: Motivates IREV5 (within-industry reversal) and RREV5/RREV21 (risk-model residual reversal) next to raw REV5.
independent_replication: Blitz, Huij, Lansdorp and Verbeek (2013) report a similar gain for residual reversal on another construction (practitioner summary only, not read in full).
limitations: Monthly reversal, 1982-2009, gross of costs; our test is daily on 2017-2026 U3000 with measured close costs.
quote: A simple short-term return reversal trading strategy designed to capture the residual component generates a highly significant risk-adjusted return three times the size of the standard reversal strategy during our 1982-2009 sampling period.

claim: Lou, Polk and Skouras (A Tug of War: Overnight Versus Intraday Expected Returns, JFE 2019): momentum profits accrue overnight and partly reverse intraday, while other anomaly returns accrue intraday, so overnight and intraday components of past returns carry different information.
impact_on_spec: Motivates ON5 and ID5 as separate inputs; the paper gives no clear sign for a 5-day component predicting total close-to-close returns, so their signs are fixed on the stress window before the recent window judges them.
independent_replication: Related: Akbas et al. 2022, Hendershott-Livdan-Rosch 2020 (not read here).
limitations: Monthly portfolios, 1993-2013; our components are 5-day means on 2017-2026.
quote: A Tug of War: Overnight Versus Intraday

claim: Avellaneda and Lee (Statistical Arbitrage in the US Equities Market, Quantitative Finance 2010): residuals of stock returns on PCA or sector-ETF factors are traded as mean-reverting processes; after transaction costs PCA-based strategies have an average annual Sharpe ratio of 1.44 over 1997-2007 but only 0.9 over 2003-2007, and ETF-based strategies 1.1 with a similar degradation after 2002.
impact_on_spec: RREV5/RREV21 use the project's risk-model residuals (industry + style factors) as the residual definition; the OU-threshold rule itself is a Stage 1 baseline, not measured here.
independent_replication: Widely replicated; recent net performance poor in Attention Factors' comparison.
limitations: 1997-2007; thresholds and costs differ from ours.
quote: during 2003-2007, the average Sharpe ratio of PCA-based strategies was only 0.9

claim: Attention Factors for statistical arbitrage (arXiv 2510.11616): with 5 bp per transaction, the parametric (OU-style) residual model falls to negative net Sharpe because of turnover, a simple PCA factor model reaches about 1.5 net, and the end-to-end model with costs in the objective reaches about 2.3 net (authors' backtest, 500 US stocks to 2021).
impact_on_spec: Shallow single-signal or threshold rules fail on costs; Stage 0 therefore measures speed curves and composites, and P1 Stage 1 puts costs into the objective.
limitations: Authors' own backtest ending 2021; flat 5 bp costs.
quote: unprecedented performance of 2.3 after trading costs

claim: Frazzini, Israel and Moskowitz (Trading Costs of Asset Pricing Anomalies, NBER draft 2012, AQR live executions): size, value and momentum survive costs at fund sizes of tens of billions, while short-term reversal does not survive at sizes above about $9 billion in the US.
impact_on_spec: Reversal is cost-constrained at institutional size but our book is small (E = $1M for impact), so the binding cost is the spread; Stage 0 uses the measured close half-spread by stock and year.
independent_replication: Consistent with Novy-Marx-Velikov; final published version not read.
limitations: Institutional execution 1998-2011; capacity, not small-account economics.
quote: Short-term reversal strategies, on the other hand, do not survive transactions costs at sizes greater than $9 billion in the U.S.

claim: Blitz, Huij, Lansdorp and Verbeek (Short-term residual reversal, Journal of Financial Markets 16(3) 2013, 477-504; abstract from the Erasmus repository record): a reversal strategy on Fama-French residual returns avoids the dynamic factor exposures of conventional reversal and earns twice its risk-adjusted return; it is significant net of trading costs even for large caps after 1990.
impact_on_spec: Second independent source for RREV5/RREV21; supports measuring residual reversal on the liquid L12 bucket with net costs.
independent_replication: Da-Liu-Schaumburg reach the same direction with a within-industry residual.
limitations: Abstract only (full text not opened: EFMA draft unreachable, SSRN not fetched); monthly horizon, sample ends about 2010.
quote: Residual reversal strategies generate statistically and economically significant profits net of trading costs, even when we restrict our sample to large-cap stocks over the post-1990 period.

claim: Avellaneda and Lee (Quantitative Finance 2010, working-paper version): on US stocks above 1 bn market cap, 60-day residual window, ETF or PCA factors, entry at 1.25 sd and exit at 0.5 sd, 5 bp per trade slippage; PCA strategies have an average annual Sharpe of 1.44 over 1997-2007 and only 0.9 in 2003-2007; ETF strategies about 1.1; volume-adjusted (trading-time) signals reach 1.51 in 2003-2007.
impact_on_spec: Fixes the PCA residual construction (top components, trailing window, standardised returns) and the volume/turnover conditioning idea; the decline after 2002 is the prior for our 2024+ window.
limitations: Authors' own backtest ending 2007, flat 5 bp per trade, no borrow cost, market cap above 1 bn only.
quote: PCA-based strategies have an average annual Sharpe ratio of 1.44 over the period 1997 to 2007

claim: Nagel (NBER w17653, Review of Financial Studies 2012): short-term reversal returns proxy the return to liquidity provision; the expected return is strongly time-varying and highly predictable with the VIX index; conditional Sharpe ratios rise with VIX in turmoil such as 2007-09.
impact_on_spec: Basis for the `vixscale` condition (scale the gross up when VIX is high relative to its trailing median).
limitations: Sample ends 2009; the VIX predictability in 2024-2026 is untested by this paper.
quote: the expected return from liquidity provision is strongly time-varying and highly predictable with the VIX index

claim: Da, Liu and Schaumburg (Management Science 60(3), 2014): the part of a past return not explained by fundamental (cash-flow) news reverses; the monthly Sharpe of the residual-based reversal is 0.52 versus 0.14 for the standard one; the effect still exists among large stocks in more recent years once the industry momentum effect is controlled for.
impact_on_spec: Supports the industry-adjusted residual and the no-news condition; the large-stock survival statement is the prior for the liquid universes.
limitations: Monthly horizon, 1982-2009 sample, analyst-revision proxy for news, not daily trading with costs.
quote: the short-term reversal effect still exists even among large stocks for the more recent years

claim: Farkas and Neszveda (EFMA 2024 draft, January 2024): short-term reversals and industry momentum arise from stocks that under-react to industry information (Laggards); long-short strategies trading Laggards double the profitability of industry momentum and short-term reversal, while the same strategies on Leader stocks are typically not profitable.
impact_on_spec: Motivates the industry-residual variant and an industry feature in the models; the Laggard proxy itself is not built here.
limitations: Working paper, monthly CRSP, sample years and post-2010 split not verified by this agent.
quote: longshort strategies trading Laggards doubles the profitability of industry momentum and short-term reversal strategies

claim: Open-source test (CRSP daily 2000-2024, survivorship-free, one-day hold, 7 bp flat cost): leave-one-out sector-residual reversal has in-sample 2000-2018 gross Sharpe 0.90 and net 0.34, and out-of-sample 2019-2024 gross 0.23 and net -0.15 (breakeven 4.2 bp); the alpha sits in short positions and low-priced names; the PCA(15) variant had no gross edge 2019-2024 (-0.07).
impact_on_spec: The strongest local prior against the family: the cheapest test is whether gross edge exists at all in 2024-2026 for liquid names, and what the measured costs do to it.
limitations: README summary through the fetch tool, code and tables not read; single author; flat cost; includes low-priced names and long/short symmetric shorts without a borrow rule.
